newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK APPROVES TIGHTER BANK LIQUIDITY RULES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK APPROVES TIGHTER BANK LIQUIDITY RULES.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Monday it had approved new measure for commercial banks, tightening the rules on their liquidity.
The new measure, which takes effect August 31, 1997, requires banks to cover liabilities with a maturity of up to one month with assets of an equal maturity "or with so-called quick liquid assets.
These include state securities, NBS liquidity bills and securities quoted on the Slovak stock exchange, the NBS said in a statement.
"Until now the NBS monitored commercial banks liquidity, but this new measure will be obligatory for banks when it takes effect," NBS spokesman Jan Onda told Reuters.

Onda did not comment on the fines or penalties the NBS could impose should a bank break the rule, nor did he disclose how often the central bank planned to control commercial banks to ensure adherence to the measure.
